utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Talic, the same question. Good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Yes, I can hear you in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Julian Nicholls with Ms. Gustin for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Nicholls. Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman along with co-counsel Milan Trbojevic and assistant Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you too. Any preliminaries before we call in the witness? Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I handed the registrar copies of our proposed sitting schedule to be given to you, and I think you have them in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: These are -- this is an agreed proposed schedule by both the Talic and Brdjanin teams. We received news from Ms. Korner this morning that she does not agree. She wants us to sit for nine straight weeks once we start on August 26th. And I will just tell you that we just can't do that. That is just beyond our physical capabilities. To sit for that many weeks in a case of this magnitude, it ignores our physical, emotional needs and everything else. The UN has rules regarding the number of hours that people are permitted to work. I tell Your Honours that when we're in session here, we work nights, we works mornings, we work afternoons, we work Saturdays, we work Sundays, we work Saturday nights, we work Sunday nights. And we don't have the kind of staff that the Prosecutor has. While Mr. Nicholls is in here doing this witness, they've got people out doing other work on the case. Everybody who works on our case is in here. And so it creates a disadvantage for the Defence to make us work a schedule of as much as nine weeks in a row. I also have -- I'm the only one who comes from miles and miles away. Everybody else in this case - and I don't mean to exclude Judge Taya, because she comes from miles and miles away too - but everyone else in this case from a lawyer standpoint could get on an airplane and go home for a weekend. I can't. I can't go home for a weekend. I have to have at least a four- or five-day break before I could justify flying all the way to Texas. And that's something I need to do. And I need to do it more often than once every eight or nine weeks. So I plead to Your Honours that this is not an unreasonable schedule. I will continue to cooperate in every way I can to make this case move forward. I've done it a lot, as you know, since we've been going along. But I do have to have these breaks. I'm -- as you pointed out, Your Honour, I'm older than you are, and you know that I have had some medical problems in this case already, and stress is not good for me. And when we get into these very, very long sessions, stress continues to be build as I get further and further behind. So I really would appreciate your consideration of this request.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We're joining the -- the motion of our learned colleague John Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll discuss it next week, and we'll -- Do you have anything to say about what Mr. Ackerman said?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No. I understand that everything that he said is quite obvious. I'm not sure if Your Honours have a proposed schedule from Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we don't have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can hand me that. Do you have a copy of Ms. Korner's --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, I only have one. I agree with Your Honours. If I can discuss it with Ms. Korner, and perhaps she can talk to the Defence and work something out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, we'll come back to you either Monday or Tuesday of next week. Thank you. Any other further preliminaries?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Not really a preliminary, Your Honour. I've just heard that Ms. Richterova is going to join me, which I'm glad of, and she will be with us soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I suppose your witness will be before -- will arrive before she does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. We can get under way. It is a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So let's prepare the courtroom for closed session. We will go into closed session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.18 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
